definition_zh: 入侵；侵略；侵犯；蜂拥而入
definition_en: the act of an army or a large number of people entering a place by force, or of something harmful spreading in
core_image: 一支队伍踏过界碑，潮水一样涌进别人的院墙
scene: 深夜的海岸线上，探照灯扫过浅滩，士兵从登陆艇上跳进水里。The islanders still tell stories of the invasion.
sceneCN: 这里 invasion 是「入侵」（第 1 个义项：武力进入他国领土），句意为岛民至今仍在讲那次入侵的故事。画面里的物件：探照灯、登陆艇、浅滩。

pos.zh: 名词：入侵；侵略；侵犯；大量涌入

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -sion 加 -de，义为「入侵；侵犯」
由本词词根加 -ive 构成，义为「侵入的；侵袭性的」
由 invade 加 -er 构成，义为「入侵者」
同带 -sion 尾的形近词，义为「逃避；回避」

senses.title: Army crossing a border
senses.definition: the act of an army entering a country with force in order to take control of it
senses.definitionCN: 军队武力进入他国、企图控制该国的行为
senses.example: The invasion began before dawn and cut the capital off within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵在黎明前开始，一天之内就切断了首都与外界的联系。
senses.why: Latin invadere meant "to go into", built from in- plus vadere, "to go".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invadere 意为「走进去」，由 in- 加 vadere「走」构成。

senses.title: Taking something over
senses.definition: the unwanted entry of a rival power into the affairs or land of another state
senses.definitionCN: 敌对势力不受欢迎地进入他国的事务或领土
senses.example: The treaty promised aid to any member facing an invasion.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承诺援助任何遭遇侵占的成员国。
senses.why: Once "go into" gained a hostile tone, the noun naturally meant a hostile entry.
senses.whyCN: 「走进去」一旦带上敌意，名词自然就指敌意的进入。

senses.title: Privacy broken into
senses.definition: an unwanted and unlawful entry into someone else's private life or space
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意且不合法地进入他人的私生活或私人空间
senses.example: Reading her letters felt like an invasion of privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 看她的信件感觉像是对隐私的侵犯。
senses.why: English extended the military noun to the borders of the self rather than of the state.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个军事名词从国家的边界挪到了个人的边界。

senses.title: A crowd or a plague
senses.definition: a large number of people or things arriving or spreading where they are not wanted
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人或事物不受欢迎地到来或蔓延
senses.example: The town is bracing for an invasion of holidaymakers in July.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇正在为七月的度假人群大批涌入做准备。
senses.why: The metaphor of a flood is old: what pours in without being asked counts as an invasion.
senses.whyCN: 「洪水」的比喻很古老：不请自来涌进来的东西都算入侵。

intro.en: Invasion comes straight from Latin invasio, a noun of "going in" onto someone else's ground.
intro.cn: invasion 直接来自拉丁语 invasio，是「走进」他人土地的名词。

items.en: The verb vadere meant "to go" and appears in many motion words.
items.cn: 动词 vadere 意为「走」，出现在许多表示移动的词中。

items.en: in- added direction to it, giving invadere, "to go into".
items.cn: in- 给它加上方向，构成 invadere「走进去」。

items.en: The noun invasio named the act of entering, often hostilely.
items.cn: 名词 invasio 指进入的行为，常带敌意。

items.en: French reshaped the noun as invasion before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语先把该名词改写成 invasion，英语再借入。

items.en: English kept the military sense and added the privacy sense in legal use.
items.cn: 英语保留军事义，又在法律用法中添了隐私义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the inva-/inve- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for hostile entry.
note.cn: 形近组共用 inva-/inve- 开头；近义组收表示敌意进入的词。

entries.definition: The act of avoiding something by trickery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「逃避」，靠花招躲开。

entries.definition: Something newly created or made up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「发明；捏造」。

entries.definition: The act of turning something upside down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「倒置」，拼写只差一个字母。

entries.definition: A sudden violent attempt to hurt or damage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「攻击」，强调突然动手。

entries.definition: A short sudden attack into enemy ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「突袭」，短促而突然。

entries.definition: An unwanted arrival into a place or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「闯入」，强调不受欢迎。

normalIntro.en: These hooks attach the word to border crossings you can picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它挂在你想象得出的越界画面上。

normal.en: in- means into, and vad- means go.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vad- 是「走」。

normal.en: in + vad + ion: the going into a place.
normal.cn: in + vad + ion：走进一个地方这件事。

normal.en: An invasion force is the group that does the going in.
normal.cn: 入侵部队就是负责走进去的那批人。

normal.en: Invasion is invasion only when the door was not opened.
normal.cn: 门不是自己打开的，才叫入侵。

normal.en: Its verb is invade, which drops the -sion.
normal.cn: 它的动词是 invade，少了 -sion 那一截。

abstract.en: Invasion is a border crossed without permission.
abstract.cn: 入侵就是一条未经许可被越过的边界。

abstract.en: When a crowd becomes a tide, the word comes out.
abstract.cn: 当人群变成潮水，这个词就出场了。

abstract.en: Privacy has borders too, and letters are a wall.
abstract.cn: 隐私也有边界，信件就是一堵墙。

examples.en: The museum closed when news of the invasion reached the city.
examples.cn: 入侵的消息传到城里，博物馆就关门了。

examples.en: Critics called the camera in the changing room an invasion of privacy.
examples.cn: 批评者称更衣室里的摄像头侵犯了隐私。

examples.en: Every summer brings an invasion of insects to the lake.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，湖边都会被虫子大批占据。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vas（走）+ ion（名词）——踩进别人的地界

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vadere「走」→ invasio「进入」→ 法语 invasion → 英语 invasion。同族有 invade、invasive、invader。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: an army crossing in, taking over another land, breaking into privacy, and a flood of people or things.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：军队越境进入、侵占他国、侵犯隐私，以及人潮物潮的大量涌入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary being crossed from the outside by force.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界被外力从外面跨过。

branches.en: THE LANDING: troops stepping onto a foreign shore.
branches.cn: 登陆这条线：士兵踏上一片异国的海岸。

branches.en: THE FLOOD: numbers that pour in without welcome.
branches.cn: 潮水这条线：不受欢迎地涌来的人与物。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a private space entered without leave.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：未经允许进入的私人空间。

branches.en: THE LINE: both senses break a boundary they were not invited past.
branches.cn: 界线这条线：两个义项都越过了没被邀请越过的界。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: both senses take what belongs to someone else.
branches.cn: 占夺这条线：两个义项都拿走了属于别人的东西。

intro.en: Invasion is in- "into", the root vad- "go", and the noun ending -sion.
intro.cn: invasion 是 in-「进入」、词根 vad-「走」与名词词尾 -sion 的组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin vadere and invasio are both recorded; the past participle invasus supplied the -s-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vadere 与 invasio 均有记载，过去分词 invasus 提供了那个 -s-。

items.example: The root survives in evade and pervade.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根仍见于 evade 与 pervade。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成动作名词。

items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor.
English kept the verb beside the noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把动词和名词并留着。
词尾 -er 指做这事的人。

items.meaning: to go out of the way
items.example: The same root with e- for out gives the opposite motion.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根配 e-「向外」就成了反向动作。

definition_en: to design and make something that did not exist before, or to make up a story or excuse
core_image: 一张空白纸上，一只手把几个零件拼成一个从没见过的东西
scene: 车间里堆着旧齿轮和铜线，一个人整夜没睡，桌上摆着刚焊好的装置。He did not invent the radio, but he made one small enough to carry.
sceneCN: 这里 invent 是「发明」（第 1 个义项：造出前所未有的东西），句意为收音机不是他发明的，但他做出了能随身携带的小型机。画面里的物件：齿轮、铜线、焊枪。

pos.zh: 动词：发明；创造；编造；虚构

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「发明；发明物」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「发明家」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「有创造力的」
同带 -vent 词干的形近词，义为「阻止」

senses.title: Making something new
senses.definition: to design and produce a device, method, or idea that no one had before
senses.definitionCN: 设计并造出此前无人有过的装置、方法或想法
senses.example: She invented a lamp that runs on salt water.
senses.exampleCN: 她发明了一盏用盐水点亮的灯。
senses.why: Latin invenire meant "to come upon", from in- plus venire, "to come".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invenire 意为「碰上」，由 in- 加 venire「来」构成。

senses.title: Creating an idea or system
senses.definition: to create a system, word, or way of doing something for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 首次创建某种体系、词语或做事方式
senses.example: The game was invented by students waiting for a train.
senses.exampleCN: 这个游戏是等火车的学生们发明的。
senses.why: Finding and founding were once the same act: you come upon a thing and it exists.
senses.whyCN: 发现与创立曾是同一件事：你碰上某物，它才算存在。

senses.title: Making up a story
senses.definition: to create characters and events in your imagination and present them as a tale
senses.definitionCN: 在想象中创造人物和事件并当作故事讲出来
senses.example: He invented a dragon that guards the library.
senses.exampleCN: 他编了一条守着图书馆的龙。
senses.why: From "come upon" the word slid to "make up", since invention and imagination share the birth of what was not there.
senses.whyCN: 从「碰上」滑到「编造」，因为发明和想象都让不在的东西诞生。

senses.title: Faking an excuse
senses.definition: to say something false in order to escape blame or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 为了逃避责备或麻烦而说出虚假的东西
senses.example: He invented a dentist appointment and left early.
senses.exampleCN: 他编了个看牙的预约，提前走了。
senses.why: The darker edge of the same power: an invented excuse is a fiction used against someone.
senses.whyCN: 同一种能力的阴暗面：编出来的借口是对付别人的虚构。

intro.en: Invent goes back to Latin invenire, "to come upon", with no hint of machines at first.
intro.cn: invent 源自拉丁语 invenire「碰上」，起初与机器无关。

items.en: The verb venire meant "to come".
items.cn: 动词 venire 意为「来」。

items.en: in- added "upon, against", giving invenire, "to come upon".
items.cn: in- 加上「向着、碰到」，构成 invenire「碰上」。

items.en: The noun inventio meant a discovery as well as a plan.
items.cn: 名词 inventio 既指发现，也指构想。

items.en: French brought the word in as inventer, "to find out".
items.cn: 法语以 inventer「找出」把词引入。

items.en: By the eighteenth century invent meant chiefly making new devices.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，invent 主要指引造新装置。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vent stem; the near-meaning group holds words for creating something new.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -vent 词干；近义组收表示创造新事物的词。

entries.definition: To stop something from happening.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「阻止」，由 pre- 加同一词干构成。

entries.definition: Something that happens.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「事件」，同一词干加 e-。

entries.definition: Acting to stop trouble before it starts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「预防的」，同词干加 -ive。

entries.definition: To bring something into existence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「创造」，范围最广。

entries.definition: To plan or design a method cleverly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「设计；想出」，偏方法。

entries.definition: To make something, often to fake it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「制造；捏造」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to the moment an idea becomes a thing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它连到「想法变成实物」的那一刻。

normal.en: in- means into, and vent- means come.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vent- 是「来」。

normal.en: To invent is to come into a new thing.
normal.cn: 发明就是走进一个此前没有的东西。

normal.en: The person who does it is the inventor.
normal.cn: 做这件事的人叫 inventor。

normal.en: The object produced is an invention.
normal.cn: 造出来的物件叫 invention。

normal.en: Invent an excuse and the same word turns against you.
normal.cn: 编个借口，同一个词就反过来伤你。

abstract.en: Invention is a path that was not on the map.
abstract.cn: 发明是一条地图上原本没有的路。

abstract.en: The empty bench and the first wheel share a yes.
abstract.cn: 空板凳和第一个轮子共享同一句「可以」。

abstract.en: A story invented is a room built where nothing stood.
abstract.cn: 编出来的故事，是在空地上盖起的一间房。

examples.en: Nobody knows who invented paper, but the idea travelled fast.
examples.cn: 没人知道纸是谁发明的，但这个主意传得很快。

examples.en: Do not invent figures to fill a gap in the report.
examples.cn: 不要编造数字去填报告里的空白。

examples.en: They invented a rule that no one could remember.
examples.cn: 他们造出一条谁也记不住的规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进来）+ vent（来）——让一个东西第一次到来

root: 拉丁语 in「进入、碰上」+ venire「来」→ invenire「碰上」→ 古法语 inventer → 英语 invent。同族有 invention、inventor、inventive；形近 prevent、event。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: building a device, founding a system, telling an imagined story, and faking an excuse.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：造出器械、创立体例、讲述想象的故事，以及捏造借口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thing comes into being where nothing stood before.
core.cn: 核心意象：在原本空无一物的地方，有东西诞生了。

branches.en: THE BENCH: a workbench where a new machine takes shape.
branches.cn: 工作台这条线：新机器在工作台上成形。

branches.en: THE RULE: a system or word that did not exist before.
branches.cn: 规则这条线：此前不存在的体例或词语。

branches.en: THE STORY: characters born inside a head.
branches.cn: 故事这条线：在头脑里诞生的人物。

branches.en: THE LIE: a fiction aimed at escaping blame.
branches.cn: 谎言这条线：用来逃避责任的虚构。

branches.en: THE SAME POWER: both senses build what is not there.
branches.cn: 同一能力：两个义项都在造不存在的东西。

intro.en: Invent is in- "into" plus the root vent- "come".
intro.cn: invent 是 in-「进入」加词根 vent-「来」。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire, inventus and inventio are all recorded members of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire、inventus 与 inventio 都是这一族有记载的成员。

items.example: It also appears in invent and prevent.
items.exampleCN: 它也见于 invent 与 prevent。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: It builds prevent, to come before and block.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prevent，提前来到并挡住。

items.example: The same stem with e- for out gives what comes out.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干配 e-「向外」指发生的事情。

definition_zh: 投资；投入（时间精力）；授予（权力）
definition_en: to put money, time, or effort into something hoping for a return, or to formally give someone power or a right
core_image: 一笔钱被装进土里，等着日后长出更多
scene: 父亲把存折推到女儿面前，让她自己决定怎么用这笔学费之外的钱。She decided to invest half of it in a small bakery.
sceneCN: 这里 invest 是「投资」（第 1 个义项：把钱投出去以求回报），句意为她决定把其中一半投进一家小面包店。画面里的物件：存折、桌面、台灯。

pos.zh: 动词：投资；投入；授予权力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「投资；投资额」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「投资者」
加前缀 di- 构成的反向词，义为「撤资；剥夺」
去掉 in- 的同源词，义为「背心；授予」

senses.title: Putting money to work
senses.definition: to put money into a business or asset in order to make a profit later
senses.definitionCN: 把钱放进企业或资产，指望日后获利
senses.example: They invested their savings in solar panels for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把积蓄投在了屋顶的太阳能板上。
senses.why: Latin investire meant "to clothe", and money clothed in a venture was said to be invested.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investire 意为「给穿衣」，钱被「穿」进一桩事业，就叫投了出去。

senses.title: Spending effort
senses.definition: to give time, energy, or attention to something because it matters
senses.definitionCN: 因为某事重要而付出时间、精力或注意力
senses.example: She invested three years in learning the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了三年时间学小提琴。
senses.why: If money can be dressed in a project, so can effort: both are resources you part with.
senses.whyCN: 钱能披挂在一个项目上，力气也行：两者都是你交出去的资源。

senses.title: Giving formal power
senses.definition: to give someone the official right or power to act in a role
senses.definitionCN: 正式赋予某人在某职位上行动的权力
senses.example: The new mayor was invested with the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长被授予聘用员工的权力。
senses.why: The oldest sense is ceremonial: a robe was put on someone to show the office was now theirs.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是仪式性的：给别人穿上礼服，表示职位从此归他。

intro.en: Invest began as a word about clothes and ceremony long before it meant money.
intro.cn: invest 在表示钱之前，长期是个关于衣服与仪式的词。

items.en: The noun vestis meant "garment".
items.cn: 名词 vestis 意为「衣服」。

items.en: investire meant "to put a garment on someone".
items.cn: investire 意为「给人穿上衣服」。

items.en: The Church used it for dressing a person in the robes of an office.
items.cn: 教会用它表示给人穿上某职位的礼服。

items.en: Trade turned the idea of clothing into placing money in a venture.
items.cn: 商业把「穿衣」的想法转成了把钱放进一桩事业。

items.en: Banks and markets fixed the financial sense in everyday speech.
items.cn: 银行与市场把这一金融义固定进了日常语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vest- stem; the near-meaning group holds words about putting resources in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vest- 词干；近义组收表示投入资源的词。

entries.definition: A sleeveless garment worn under a jacket.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「背心」，同词根。

entries.definition: To sell off holdings or strip someone of power.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「撤资；剥夺」，反向词。

entries.definition: To create something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」，拼写只差一个字母。

entries.definition: To provide money for a project.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「资助」，提供资金。

entries.definition: To give time or attention completely to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「奉献」，强调全心全意。

entries.definition: To set money or resources aside for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「拨出」，指分配。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move the word from a robe to a wallet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个词从礼服挪到钱包。

normal.en: in- means in, and vest- means clothes.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vest- 是「衣服」。

normal.en: Money is dressed in a project, so it is invested.
normal.cn: 钱被「穿」在项目上，所以叫投进去。

normal.en: What you put in is an investment.
normal.cn: 你放进去的那笔就叫 investment。

normal.en: The person who puts it in is an investor.
normal.cn: 放进去的人叫 investor。

normal.en: Dress effort in a cause and you invest in it too.
normal.cn: 把力气披挂在一件事上，也是 invest。

abstract.en: Investment is trust wearing a price tag.
abstract.cn: 投资是贴上价签的信任。

abstract.en: To invest is to plant and then leave the field alone.
abstract.cn: 投资是种下去，然后先别去动那块地。

abstract.en: Power, like money, is handed over by an act of dressing.
abstract.cn: 权力和钱一样，都靠一个「加衣」的动作交出去。

examples.en: The fund invests mainly in small farms.
examples.cn: 这只基金主要投资小型农场。

examples.en: He invested every spare hour in the repair of the boat.
examples.cn: 他把每一个空闲小时都投在了修船上。

examples.en: The board invested the director with full control of the budget.
examples.cn: 董事会授予这位主管完全的预算控制权。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vest（衣服）——把钱裹进项目里

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestis「衣服」→ investire「给穿衣」→ 中世纪拉丁语指授职 → 英语 invest 引申为「投资」。同族有 investment、investor、divest、vest。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: putting in money, putting in effort, and formally granting power.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：投入金钱、投入精力，以及正式授予权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something valuable is handed over and dressed in a new role.
core.cn: 核心意象：有价值的东西被交出去，并披上一个新的身份。

branches.en: THE PURSE: money placed where it can grow.
branches.cn: 钱包这条线：放在能生长之处的钱。

branches.en: THE HOURS: time given to a craft or cause.
branches.cn: 时间这条线：给一门手艺或一件事的时间。

branches.en: THE ROBE: official authority put on a person.
branches.cn: 礼服这条线：披在某人身上的官方权力。

branches.en: THE RESOURCE: both senses part with something now for later.
branches.cn: 资源这条线：两个义项都是现在付出、以后收获。

branches.en: THE GRANT: both senses make a formal transfer of value.
branches.cn: 授予这条线：两个义项都完成一次正式的价值转移。

intro.en: Invest is in- "into" plus vestis "garment"; the robe may be worn by a man or by money.
intro.cn: invest 是 in-「进入」加 vestis「衣服」，穿上礼服的可能是人，也可能是钱。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis, vestire and investire are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis、vestire 与 investire 均有记载。

items.example: The root names what is put on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被穿上的东西。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: The bare stem still names a piece of clothing.
items.exampleCN: 光词干至今仍指一件衣服。

items.example: It builds divest, to strip away.

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把方向反了过来。

definition_en: a careful, formal attempt to find out the facts about an event, problem, or claim
core_image: 手电照着地面，一步步顺着脚印往里查
scene: 办公室里文件摊满桌面，两个人对着账本逐页核对日期。The investigation found that two payments had been recorded twice.
sceneCN: 这里 investigation 是「调查」（第 1 个义项：为弄清事实而做的正式查证），句意为调查发现有两笔付款被记了两次。画面里的物件：账本、桌面、荧光笔。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 换 -ate，义为「调查；侦查」
由 investigate 加 -or 构成，义为「调查员」
由 investigate 词干加 -ive 构成，义为「调查性的」

senses.title: Official fact-finding
senses.definition: a formal process in which an authority examines evidence to establish the truth
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构审查证据、确定真相的正式过程
senses.example: A government investigation cleared the factory of any fault.
senses.exampleCN: 政府调查澄清这家工厂没有过错。
senses.why: Latin investigare meant "to follow the footprints", from in- plus vestigium, "track".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investigare 意为「跟着脚印走」，由 in- 加 vestigium「足迹」构成。

senses.title: Police or detective work
senses.definition: the work of police or detectives gathering facts about a suspected crime
senses.definitionCN: 警方或侦探就疑似犯罪收集事实的工作
senses.example: The investigation into the missing paintings lasted four years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失踪画作的侦查持续了四年。
senses.why: The footprint image fits best here: a detective literally follows a trail.
senses.whyCN: 「脚印」这个意象在这里最贴切：侦探就是顺着痕迹走的人。

senses.title: Careful study of a problem
senses.definition: a thorough academic or scientific study of a question
senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题所作的详尽学术或科学研究
senses.example: Her investigation of soil bacteria changed the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她对土壤细菌的研究改变了这个领域。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word because a good study also follows traces until a pattern shows.
senses.whyCN: 科学借用了这个词，因为好的研究同样顺着痕迹走到规律显现。

intro.en: Investigation carries a picture of footprints: Latin vestigium means "track".
intro.cn: investigation 带着脚印的画面：拉丁语 vestigium 意为「足迹」。

items.en: vestigium meant "footprint, trace".
items.cn: vestigium 意为「脚印、痕迹」。

items.en: investigare meant "to follow a track".
items.cn: investigare 意为「跟着足迹走」。

items.en: The noun investigatio named the search itself.
items.cn: 名词 investigatio 指这场追寻。

items.en: English took the noun for legal and official enquiries.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词用于法律与官方查问。

items.en: Science adopted it for systematic study as well.
items.cn: 科学界也采用它表示系统性研究。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vestigi- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for searching out facts.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vestigi- 词干；近义组收表示查明事实的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to look into a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调查」，同词干。

entries.definition: Money put in for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资」，开头相同。

entries.definition: A request to come somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「邀请」，尾音相近。

entries.definition: A question or a formal look into facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「询问；查问」。

entries.definition: A close and often official examination.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「探查」，常指官方深入检查。

entries.definition: Systematic study to discover new facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「研究」，偏学术。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all walk along a set of footprints.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都沿着同一串脚印走。

normal.en: in- means into, and vestigium means footprint.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vestigium 是「脚印」。

normal.en: To investigate is to follow the prints in.
normal.cn: investigate 就是顺着脚印往里查。

normal.en: The noun investigation is the whole walk.
normal.cn: 名词 investigation 指这整段路。

normal.en: An investigator is the one holding the torch.
normal.cn: investigator 是那个举着手电的人。

normal.en: Under investigation means the trail is still warm.
normal.cn: under investigation 意思是痕迹还热着。

abstract.en: Investigation is doubt that refuses to stay lazy.
abstract.cn: 调查是不肯偷懒的怀疑。

abstract.en: Every fact leaves a footprint; the word is the act of bending down.
abstract.cn: 每个事实都留下脚印；这个词就是弯腰去看。

abstract.en: A careful inquiry turns noise into a line.
abstract.cn: 仔细的查证把杂音拉成一条线。

examples.en: The investigation into the fire took almost a year.
examples.cn: 对那场火灾的调查花了将近一年。

examples.en: Two officers were suspended while under investigation.
examples.cn: 两名警员在接受调查期间被停职。

examples.en: Her investigation of the lake water found traces of lead.
examples.cn: 她对湖水的调查发现了微量的铅。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vestig（脚印）+ ation（名词）——顺着脚印查到底

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestigium「足迹」→ investigare「跟踪追查」→ investigatio → 英语 investigation。同族有 investigate、investigator、investigative。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an official inquiry, police detective work, and a thorough study of a question.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：官方查证、警方侦查，以及对某个问题的深入研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: following a trail of footprints until the truth shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：顺着脚印走，直到真相显现。

branches.en: THE FILE: officials checking records against facts.
branches.cn: 档案这条线：官员把记录与事实对照。

branches.en: THE TRAIL: detectives walking a case to its end.
branches.cn: 痕迹这条线：侦探把一个案子走到底。

branches.en: THE LAB: researchers chasing a pattern through data.
branches.cn: 实验室这条线：研究者在数据里追一个规律。

branches.en: THE PROOF: both senses need evidence that holds up.
branches.cn: 证据这条线：两个义项都要站得住的证据。

branches.en: THE METHOD: both senses proceed step by step.
branches.cn: 方法这条线：两个义项都一步一步推进。

intro.en: Investigation is in- "into", vestigium "track", -ate the verb ending, and -ion for the act.
intro.cn: investigation 由 in-「进入」、vestigium「足迹」、动词尾 -ate 与名词尾 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium and investigare are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium 与 investigare 均有记载。

items.example: It marks walking inward along a trace.
The root is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是这个词的心脏。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
The bare root still names a trace left behind.
items.exampleCN: 光词根仍指留下的痕迹。

definition_zh: 无敌的；不能战胜的；难以动摇的
definition_en: too strong to be defeated or overcome, either in battle or in spirit
core_image: 一面盾牌被反复砍击，却连一道划痕也没留下
scene: 球场上主队连赢一整个赛季，对手在赛前就开始心里发怯。For three months the team looked invincible.
sceneCN: 这里 invincible 是「不可战胜的」（第 1 个义项：强大到打不败），句意为这支球队有三个月看起来无人可敌。画面里的物件：球场、记分牌、球衣。

pos.zh: 形容词：无敌的；不能战胜的；难以动摇的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「无敌；不可战胜」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「不可战胜地」
去掉否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「可被战胜的」
同带 vinc- 词根的形近词，义为「说服」

senses.title: Undefeated in battle
senses.definition: so strong that no enemy can defeat it
senses.definitionCN: 强大到没有任何敌人能够击败
senses.example: For a century the fortress was thought invincible.
senses.exampleCN: 一个世纪里，这座要塞都被认为攻不破。
senses.why: Latin vincere meant "to conquer", and in- here simply negates it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vincere 意为「征服」，这里的 in- 只是把它否定掉。

senses.title: Unbeatable in a contest
senses.definition: performing so well that rivals cannot win against you
senses.definitionCN: 表现好到对手无法取胜
senses.example: The chess champion seemed invincible until a schoolgirl beat him.
senses.exampleCN: 这位象棋冠军似乎无人能敌，直到一个女学生赢了他。
senses.why: Sport and games borrowed the military word whenever a record held.
senses.whyCN: 体育与游戏在纪录无人打破时就借来这个军事词。

senses.title: Unshakable in feeling
senses.definition: too firm in courage or belief to be weakened by setbacks
senses.definitionCN: 勇气或信念坚定到挫折也无法削弱
senses.example: She went into the hearing with invincible calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着不可动摇的镇定走进听证会。
senses.why: The word moved from the body to the mind: what cannot be beaten inside is also invincible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从身体挪到心灵：内里打不败的东西也是无敌的。

intro.en: Invincible is the Latin negative in- joined to vincibilis, "able to be overcome".
intro.cn: invincible 是拉丁否定前缀 in- 加上 vincibilis「可被战胜的」。

items.en: vincere meant "to conquer, to prevail".
items.cn: vincere 意为「征服、取胜」。

items.en: The adjective vincibilis meant "can be overcome".
items.cn: 形容词 vincibilis 意为「可被战胜的」。

items.en: Adding in- produced invincibilis, "not to be overcome".
items.cn: 加 in- 构成 invincibilis「不可战胜的」。

items.en: French passed the word on as invincible.
items.cn: 法语以 invincible 把它传出。

items.en: English applied it to armies first, then to minds and arguments.
items.cn: 英语先用它说军队，后来说心志与论点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vinc- root; the near-meaning group holds words for being unbeatable.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vinc- 词根；近义组收表示不可击败的词。

entries.definition: To make someone believe something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「说服」，同词根。

entries.definition: Able to be defeated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「可战胜的」，少了否定前缀。

entries.definition: Impossible to see.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「看不见的」，只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Impossible to beat in a contest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「无法击败的」，偏口语。

entries.definition: Never to be taken by force.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不可征服的」，偏书面。

entries.definition: Spirit that cannot be tamed or broken.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不屈不挠的」，多指精神。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into a no plus a conquer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它拆成一个「不」加一个「征服」。

normal.en: in- means not, and vinc- means conquer.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，vinc- 是「征服」。

normal.en: Invincible is literally unconquerable.
normal.cn: invincible 字面上就是不可征服。

normal.en: Take off in- and you get vincible, which no army wants.
normal.cn: 去掉 in- 就得到 vincible，没有军队想当。

normal.en: Winners in one long season get called invincible.
normal.cn: 连赢一整个赛季的队伍就被叫无敌。

normal.en: Vinc- also hides in convince, where you conquer a doubt.
normal.cn: vinc- 也藏在 convince 里，征服的是怀疑。

abstract.en: Invincibility is a mirror that only looks one way.
abstract.cn: 无敌是一面只朝一个方向照的镜子。

abstract.en: A shield with no scratch is also a shield with no story.
abstract.cn: 没有划痕的盾，也没有故事。

abstract.en: The calm that cannot be shaken is the quiet kind of victory.
abstract.cn: 摇不动的镇定，是安静的一种胜利。

examples.en: No army is truly invincible, however many battles it wins.
examples.cn: 无论赢多少场仗，没有军队真能无敌。

examples.en: The old champion looked invincible until the second round.
examples.cn: 那位老冠军看起来无人能敌，直到第二轮就败了。

examples.en: She faced the crowd with invincible confidence.
examples.cn: 她以不可动摇的自信面对人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vinc（征服）+ ible（能……的）——没能被征服的

root: 拉丁语 vincere「征服」→ vincibilis「可被战胜的」→ 加否定前缀 in- 成 invincibilis → 英语 invincible。同族有 vincible、invincibility、convince。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: undefeated in war, unbeatable in competition, and unshakable in spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：战场不可战胜、比赛无人能胜，以及精神上不可动摇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shield that takes every blow and shows no mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：挨了所有打击却毫无痕迹的盾牌。

branches.en: THE FORTRESS: walls no siege can break.
branches.cn: 要塞这条线：围城攻不破的墙。

branches.en: THE STREAK: a record that keeps holding.
branches.cn: 连胜这条线：一直没人打破的纪录。

branches.en: THE NERVE: courage that setbacks cannot dent.
branches.cn: 心志这条线：挫折也压不垮的勇气。

branches.en: THE TEST: both senses are judged by someone attacking.
branches.cn: 考验这条线：两个义项都要有人来攻才显出来。

branches.en: THE REVIEW: rivals and doubts are the same kind of pressure.
branches.cn: 审视这条线：对手与怀疑是同一种压力。

intro.en: Invincible is in- "not" plus vinc- "conquer" plus -ible "able to be".
intro.cn: invincible 是 in-「不」加 vinc-「征服」再加 -ible「能被……的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vincere and invincibilis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vincere 与 invincibilis 均有记载。

items.example: It flips the meaning of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词的意思翻过来。

items.example: The root also appears in convince.
It forms vincible, able to be beaten.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 vincible，能被战胜的。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: A cousin of the same root with a different spelling.
items.exampleCN: 同词根的表亲，拼写略异。

items.example: Here the conquering happens inside another mind.
items.exampleCN: 在这里，征服发生在别人的脑子里。

definition_zh: 看不见的；无形的；不受注意的
definition_en: not able to be seen because it is too small, too far, clear, or simply unnoticed
core_image: 一块玻璃立在空地上，人一走过去就消失在里面
scene: 实验台上一支玻璃管里冒气，肉眼什么都看不出来。The gas is invisible, but it turns the litmus paper blue.
sceneCN: 这里 invisible 是「看不见的」（第 1 个义项：眼睛无法察觉），句意为这种气体看不见，却能让蓝色石蕊试纸变色。画面里的物件：玻璃管、石蕊试纸、手套。

pos.zh: 形容词：看不见的；无形的；不受注意的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「隐形；不可见性」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「无形地」
去掉否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「看得见的」
同带 vis- 词根的形近词，义为「视力；远见」

senses.title: Cannot be seen
senses.definition: impossible for the eye to notice because of size, distance, or colourlessness
senses.definitionCN: 因为太小、太远或没有颜色而无法被眼睛察觉
senses.example: The bacteria are invisible without a microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 没有显微镜，这些细菌是看不见的。
senses.why: Latin videre meant "to see"; in- negatives the verb visibilis comes from.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre 意为「看见」，in- 把 visibilis 所自的动词否定掉。

senses.title: Wrongly ignored
senses.definition: present but not noticed or counted by people who should care
senses.definitionCN: 实际存在却被本该关心的人忽略或不算在内
senses.example: Older carers often feel invisible to the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的照护者常觉得在医疗体系里没人看见他们。
senses.why: Social use takes the eye metaphor into institutions: what is not counted is not seen.
senses.whyCN: 社会用法把眼睛的比喻带进制度：没被统计的，就等于没被看见。

senses.title: Not obvious in money or power
senses.definition: hidden in form but real in effect, like costs or forces
senses.definitionCN: 形式上隐藏、实际却有效果，如成本或力量
senses.example: Every purchase carries invisible costs for the river.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次购买都为这条河带来看不见的代价。
senses.why: Accounts talk about invisible balances when the effect is real but the form is not on the page.
senses.whyCN: 账目里的「无形」余额，说的是效果真实、却不写在纸面上。

intro.en: Invisible is Latin in- "not" plus visibilis, "that can be seen", from videre "to see".
intro.cn: invisible 是拉丁 in-「不」加 visibilis「可见的」，后者来自 videre「看」。

items.en: videre meant "to see".
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」。

items.en: visibilis meant "able to be seen".
items.cn: visibilis 意为「能被看见的」。

items.en: in- negated it to invisibilis, "not visible".
items.cn: in- 将其否定为 invisibilis「看不见的」。

items.en: French carried the adjective into English forms.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词带入英语形式。

items.en: Science and economics borrowed it for gases, germs, and hidden costs.
items.cn: 科学与经济学借它说气体、细菌与隐性成本。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vis- root; the near-meaning group holds words for what cannot be noticed.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vis- 词根；近义组收表示无法察觉的词。

entries.definition: Able to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「可见的」，只少否定前缀。

entries.definition: Impossible to defeat.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不可战胜的」，拼写只差两个字母。

entries.definition: Related to sight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「视觉的」，同词根。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「隐藏的」，多为有意。

entries.definition: Not noticed by anyone watching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「未被看见的」，偏观察角度。

entries.definition: Real but impossible to touch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「无形的」，强调摸不着。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word tied to the small prefix that says no.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它系在那个表示「不」的小前缀上。

normal.en: in- says not, and visible says able to be seen.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，visible 是「能被看见」。

normal.en: Glass is visible only by its edge.
normal.cn: 玻璃只有靠边缘才看得出来。

normal.en: Invisible ink has to be warmed to show up.
normal.cn: 隐形墨水要加热才显现。

normal.en: Remove in- and the word turns into its exact opposite.
normal.cn: 去掉 in-，这个词就变成它的正相反。

normal.en: A person can be invisible without vanishing.
normal.cn: 人可以不消失，却「不被看见」。

abstract.en: Invisibility is a matter of who is looking, not only of what is there.
abstract.cn: 无形不只取决于有没有东西，还取决于谁在看。

abstract.en: Some costs never appear on the receipt.
abstract.cn: 有些代价永远不会出现在小票上。

abstract.en: The ignored are the truest invisible ones.
abstract.cn: 被忽略的人，才是最彻底的无形。

examples.en: Ultraviolet light is invisible but burns the skin.
examples.cn: 紫外线看不见，却会晒伤皮肤。

examples.en: The seam was made invisible with tiny stitches.
examples.cn: 那道缝用极细的针脚做成了看不见的。

examples.en: Cleaners work at night and stay invisible to most staff.
examples.cn: 保洁员夜里工作，对大多数员工来说一直「看不见」。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vis（看）+ ible（能……的）——看不到的

root: 拉丁语 in-「不」+ videre「看」→ visibilis「可见的」→ invisibilis → 英语 invisible。同族有 visible、vision、visual、invisibility。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: hidden from the eye, ignored by people, and real but not obvious.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：肉眼看不见、被人忽视，以及真实却不显形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is there, but the eye slides past it.
core.cn: 核心意象：东西就在那里，眼睛却滑过去了。

branches.en: THE GLASS: clear things that show only at the edge.
branches.cn: 玻璃这条线：只在边缘显形的透明物。

branches.en: THE COUNT: people left out of the numbers.
branches.cn: 统计这条线：被数字落下的人。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: forces with real weight and no line on the page.
branches.cn: 账本这条线：真有分量却没有条目的力量。

branches.en: THE EYE: both senses depend on someone failing to notice.
branches.cn: 眼睛这条线：两个义项都取决于有人没留意到。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: institutions decide what becomes visible.
branches.cn: 制度这条线：是制度决定什么能被看见。

intro.en: Invisible is in- "not", vis- "see", and -ible "able to be".
intro.cn: invisible 是 in-「不」、vis-「看」与 -ible「能被……的」三段。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and invisibilis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 invisibilis 均有记载。

items.example: It flips visible into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它把 visible 翻成反义。

items.example: The root also appears in vision and visual.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 vision 与 visual。

items.example: It forms visible, able to be seen.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 visible，能被看见的。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.meaning: sight or a plan seen ahead

items.example: Same root with an adjective ending.

definition_zh: 邀请；招待；招致（麻烦、批评）
definition_en: to ask someone to come somewhere or do something, or to make something likely to happen
core_image: 一扇门被推开，主人朝外伸出手做个「请进」的姿势
scene: 周末的厨房里炖着汤，主人擦擦手，走到门口朝对面的邻居招手。She invited the whole street to dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 invite 是「邀请」（第 1 个义项：请别人来），句意为她请了整条街的人来吃晚饭。画面里的物件：汤锅、门口、手巾。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「邀请；邀请函」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「诱人的」
由本词加 -ee 构成，义为「被邀请者」
由本词加 -ional 构成，义为「邀请制的」

senses.title: Asking someone to come
senses.definition: to ask a person politely to come to an event or a place
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请人到某个活动或某个地方来
senses.example: They invited us to the wedding in June.
senses.exampleCN: 他们邀请我们参加六月的婚礼。
senses.why: Latin invitare meant "to ask, to entertain", with no need for a written card.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invitare 意为「邀请、款待」，那时还不需要请柬。

senses.title: Offering hospitality
senses.definition: to receive someone as a guest and provide food or lodging
senses.definitionCN: 把某人当客人接来，并提供饭食或住处
senses.example: A neighbour invited the stranded family in for tea.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居把滞留的那家人请进屋喝茶。
senses.why: The same verb covers the welcome itself, not just the asking.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也涵盖「招待」这件事，而不只是开口请。

senses.title: Bringing trouble on yourself
senses.definition: to make something bad or unwanted more likely by your own action
senses.definitionCN: 因为自己的举动让不好的事情更容易发生
senses.example: Leaving the gate open invites trouble at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里不关院门是会招来麻烦的。
senses.why: The "trouble" sense is the welcoming gesture aimed at something harmful.
senses.whyCN: 「招麻烦」义就是同一个欢迎手势，只是指向了有害的东西。

senses.title: Welcoming a response
senses.definition: to openly welcome comments, questions, or applications
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示乐于接受意见、提问或报名
senses.example: The paper invites readers to send in photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸欢迎读者寄来照片。
senses.why: A request for replies is still an invitation, only written to many at once.
senses.whyCN: 征集回应仍是邀请，只不过一次写给许多人。

intro.en: Invite has kept its original meaning of asking and welcoming almost unchanged for two thousand years.
intro.cn: invite 两千年来几乎原封不动地保留了「邀请、款待」的原意。

items.en: invitare meant "to ask, to treat as a guest".
items.cn: invitare 意为「邀请、当客人款待」。

items.en: The noun invitatus recorded the welcoming of a guest.
items.cn: 名词 invitatus 记载了对客人的接待。

items.en: French had inviter, used for asking someone over.
items.cn: 法语有 inviter，用于请人过来。

items.en: English shortened the French verb to invite.
items.cn: 英语把法语动词缩成 invite。

items.en: The sense of inviting trouble grew from the idea of welcoming.
items.cn: 「招来麻烦」义从「迎接」的想法里长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invi- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for asking people in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invi- 开头；近义组收表示请人进来的词。

entries.definition: A spoken or written request to come.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「邀请；请柬」，同族词。

entries.definition: To put money or effort in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」，开头相同。

entries.definition: To make something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」，只差一个字母。

entries.definition: The general verb for requesting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「请；问」，最泛。

entries.definition: To greet someone with pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「欢迎」，强调态度。

entries.definition: To order someone to come.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「传唤」，带命令色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks put the word at a door being held open.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它放在一扇被扶开的门口。

normal.en: The old verb invitare meant to ask and to treat well.
normal.cn: 古动词 invitare 既指邀请，也指好好招待。

normal.en: What arrives in the post is an invitation.
normal.cn: 寄到手里的东西叫 invitation。

normal.en: The person who receives it is the invitee.
normal.cn: 收到邀请的人叫 invitee。

normal.en: Leave a door open and you invite the wind.
normal.cn: 门留着不关，就是把风请进来。

normal.en: Invite a question and you are glad to hear it.
normal.cn: invite questions 就是欢迎别人提问。

abstract.en: Invitation is a door left open on purpose.
abstract.cn: 邀请就是一扇有意留开的门。

abstract.en: Whatever you welcome decides what follows you home.
abstract.cn: 你欢迎什么，什么就跟你回家。

abstract.en: Inviting trouble is the same gesture, aimed badly.
abstract.cn: 招麻烦是同一个手势，只是指错了方向。

examples.en: She invited two former students back to speak at the school.
examples.cn: 她请了两位往届学生回校演讲。

examples.en: The narrow path invites people to walk faster than they should.
examples.cn: 这条窄路会引诱人走得比该有的速度快。

examples.en: The magazine invites letters from readers of any age.
examples.cn: 这本杂志欢迎任何年龄的读者来信。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进来）+ vite（拉丁 invitare 邀请）——请你进来

root: 拉丁语 invitare「邀请；款待」→ 古法语 inviter → 英语 invite。同族有 invitation、invitee、inviting。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: asking someone over, receiving a guest, drawing trouble, and welcoming replies.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：请人来、招待客人、招来麻烦，以及欢迎回应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out as the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：门开时伸出的那只手。

branches.en: THE CARD: a written or spoken request to come.
branches.cn: 请柬这条线：写出来或说出口的请。

branches.en: THE TABLE: food and shelter given to a guest.
branches.cn: 饭桌这条线：给客人的饭食与住处。

branches.en: THE GATE: an open entry that lets trouble in.
branches.cn: 院门这条线：留开的通道把麻烦放进来。

branches.en: THE OPENNESS: both senses come from a willing yes.
branches.cn: 敞开这条线：两个义项都源于一个乐意的「好」。

branches.en: THE RESULT: what you welcome decides what arrives.
branches.cn: 结果这条线：你欢迎什么，就决定什么到来。

intro.en: Invite keeps a single Latin stem, invit-, plus the verb ending -e.
intro.cn: invite 由一个拉丁词干 invit- 加动词尾 -e 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin invitare and invitatus are both recorded with the friendly sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 invitare 与 invitatus 均有记载，都带友好的意味。

items.example: The root survives in invite and invitation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根仍见于 invite 与 invitation。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
The participle shows the noun form.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词显示名词形式。

definition_en: to include someone or something as a necessary part, or to draw a person into an activity or problem
core_image: 一张卷起的纸，把旁边的东西一层层包进去
scene: 事故现场拉着警戒线，几个路过的人也被记录成了证人。The delay involved three separate repairs and two inspections.
sceneCN: 这里 involve 是「涉及」（第 1 个义项：把某事作为组成部分包含在内），句意为这次延误涉及三轮维修和两次检查。画面里的物件：警戒线、记录本、铁皮。

pos.zh: 动词：涉及；包含；使卷入；需要

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「参与；牵连」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「复杂的；有关的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「引人入胜的」
同带 volv- 词根的形近词，义为「进化；演变」

senses.title: Having something as a part
senses.definition: to include something as a necessary part of a process or situation
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为过程或情形中必要的一部分包含进来
senses.example: The job involves long hours in cold rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作需要长时间待在冷库里。
senses.why: involvere rolled things inside; a job that includes a task has rolled the task in.
senses.whyCN: involvere 是把东西卷在里面；一份工作含有某项任务，就是把它卷了进来。

senses.title: Drawing people in
senses.definition: to make someone take part in or be affected by something
senses.definitionCN: 使人参与某事或受到某事影响
senses.example: The decision involved every member of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定牵涉到村里的每一个人。
senses.why: People wrapped into a matter are involved parties, whether they wished it or not.
senses.whyCN: 被卷进一件事的人就是当事方，愿不愿意都一样。

senses.title: Being complicated
senses.definition: to become difficult because many parts are tangled together
senses.definitionCN: 因为许多部分缠在一起而变得难以处理
senses.example: The case grew more involved with each new witness.
senses.exampleCN: 随着新证人出现，这个案子变得越来越复杂。
senses.why: Many threads rolled tight make a knot: that is the complicated sense.
senses.whyCN: 许多线被紧紧卷在一起就成了结，这就是「复杂」那一层。

intro.en: Involve comes from Latin involvere, "to roll up, to wrap", which is literally a paper rolled around something.
intro.cn: involve 来自拉丁语 involvere「卷起、包裹」，字面就是纸把东西卷进去。

items.en: The verb volvere meant "to roll".
items.cn: 动词 volvere 意为「滚、卷」。

items.en: in- added the idea of inward motion, giving involvere, "to roll in".
items.cn: in- 加上向内，构成 involvere「卷进去」。

items.en: The verb was used of wrapping things in cloth or mist.
items.cn: 这个词被用来指用布或雾把东西包起来。

items.en: French took it in as involver, "to wrap up".
items.cn: 法语以 involver「包裹」吸收它。

items.en: The wrapped sense turned into the social sense of being entangled in a matter.
items.cn: 「包住」义转成在社会事务中被缠住的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -volve stem; the near-meaning group holds words for including or entangling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -volve 词干；近义组收表示包含或牵连的词。

entries.definition: To develop gradually over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「演变」，同一词干换前缀。

entries.definition: To turn around a centre.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「旋转」，同词干。

entries.definition: Complicated, or taking part in something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「复杂的；有关的」，同族词。

entries.definition: To have something as part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「包括」，最中性。

entries.definition: To make something necessary as a result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「必然涉及」，偏后果。

entries.definition: To twist into a complicated situation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「缠住」，偏麻烦。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all start with a sheet of paper being rolled up.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都从一张被卷起的纸开始。

normal.en: in- means in, and volv- means roll.
normal.cn: in- 是「向内」，volv- 是「卷」。

normal.en: Involve is to roll something into the middle.
normal.cn: involve 就是把东西卷到里面去。

normal.en: What gets rolled in is involved in the affair.
normal.cn: 被卷进去的，就是牵扯其中的。

normal.en: Revolve rolls around an axis; evolve rolls out.
normal.cn: revolve 绕轴卷，evolve 向外卷开。

normal.en: Adding -ment gives the state of involvement.
normal.cn: 加 -ment 就是 involvement 这个状态。

abstract.en: To involve is to fold someone into the story.
abstract.cn: involve 就是把某人褶进这个故事里。

abstract.en: Every wrapped thing has edges you did not plan.
abstract.cn: 每一个被包住的东西都有你没算到的折角。

abstract.en: Complication is many threads rolled tight.
abstract.cn: 复杂就是许多线被紧紧卷在一起。

examples.en: The repair involves replacing the whole pump.
examples.cn: 这次维修要更换整个水泵。

examples.en: Parents were involved in planning the new playground.
examples.cn: 家长参与了新游乐场的筹划。

examples.en: Keep the story simple; the readers do not want an involved plot.
examples.cn: 故事写简单些，读者不想要错综复杂的情节。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ volve（卷）——被卷进来

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ volvere「卷」→ involvere「卷进去、包裹」→ 古法语 involver → 英语 involve。同族有 involvement、involved；形近 revolve、evolve。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: including a part, drawing people in, and becoming tangled and complex.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：包含组成部分、把人牵进来，以及变得盘根错节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet rolled inward until other things are inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸向内卷起，把别的东西也裹了进去。

branches.en: THE STEPS: what a job or plan must contain.
branches.cn: 步骤这条线：一份工作或计划必须含有的环节。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: everyone rolled into the matter.
branches.cn: 人物这条线：被卷进这件事的所有人。

branches.en: THE KNOT: a case too tangled to explain quickly.
branches.cn: 绳结这条线：复杂到一时说不清的案子。

branches.en: THE WEB: parts and people are bound by the same thread.
branches.cn: 网这条线：组成部分与人被同一根线连着。

branches.en: THE COST: drawing people in is what makes things complicated.
branches.cn: 代价这条线：把人牵进来，事情才变复杂。

intro.en: Involve is in- "into" plus volv- "roll".
intro.cn: involve 是 in-「进入」加 volv-「卷」。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere and involvere are both recorded roll-words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 与 involvere 都是有记载的「卷」类词。

items.example: The root also drives revolve and evolve.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也带动 revolve 与 evolve。

items.example: It forms involved, tangled or related.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 involved，纠结或有关的。
它构成 involving，引人入胜的。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: The re- prefix sends it around.
The e- prefix rolls it outward.
items.exampleCN: e- 前缀把它向外卷开。

definition_en: the state of taking part in something or of being connected with it, often as a matter of responsibility
core_image: 一只手伸进正在运转的机器里，成了它的一部分
scene: 社区中心墙上贴着排班表，好几位老人每周都来分菜。Her involvement in the food bank began with one afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 involvement 是「参与」（第 1 个义项：主动投入某项活动），句意为她在食品银行的参与从某一个下午开始。画面里的物件：排班表、菜筐、记号笔。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ment 构成，义为「涉及；使卷入」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「参与的；复杂的」
同以 in- 开头、invol- 词干的形近词，义为「非自愿的」

senses.title: Taking an active part
senses.definition: the fact of actively giving your time or effort to an activity
senses.definitionCN: 主动把时间或精力投入到某项活动中的事实
senses.example: Her involvement in the choir gave her a way to make friends.
senses.exampleCN: 参加合唱团让她找到了交朋友的方式。
senses.why: The -ment noun turns the act of joining in into a lasting relation.
senses.whyCN: -ment 名词把「加入」这个动作变成一种持续的关系。

senses.title: Being connected to a trouble
senses.definition: the state of being linked to an accident, crime, or scandal
senses.definitionCN: 与事故、犯罪或丑闻被联系在一起的状态
senses.example: He denied any involvement in the theft.
senses.exampleCN: 他否认与这起盗窃有任何牵连。
senses.why: Here the wrapping is unwanted: a name rolled into a police file.
senses.whyCN: 这里的包裹是不情愿的：一个名字被卷进了警方的卷宗。

senses.title: Emotional commitment
senses.definition: a deep personal interest or feeling that makes leaving hard
senses.definitionCN: 一种让人难以抽身的深切私人兴趣或情感
senses.example: Her emotional involvement in the case tested her judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个案子的情感投入影响了她的判断。
senses.why: Feeling can be wrapped in too, and that is the heaviest kind of involvement.
senses.whyCN: 情感也会被卷进去，那是最沉的一种投入。

intro.en: Involvement is the noun from involve, which began as Latin involvere, "to wrap".
intro.cn: involvement 是 involve 的名词，而 involve 起初就是拉丁 involvere「包裹」。

items.en: volvere meant "to roll".
items.cn: volvere 意为「滚、卷」。

items.en: involvere meant "to roll in, to wrap".
items.cn: involvere 意为「卷进、包裹」。

items.en: French passed the verb in as involver.
items.cn: 法语以 involver 传入这个动词。

items.en: English added -ment to name the state of being wrapped in.
items.cn: 英语加 -ment 指「被包进去」的状态。

items.en: Modern usage splits the noun into participation and complicity.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个名词分成「参与」与「牵连」两面。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the involv- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for taking part.
note.cn: 形近组共用 involv- 词干；近义组收表示参与的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to include or entangle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「涉及；卷入」，同族词。

entries.definition: Money put in for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资」，开头相近。

entries.definition: Done without a choice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「非自愿的」，同前缀。

entries.definition: The act of taking part in something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「参与」，最直接的对等词。

entries.definition: A promise and the effort to keep it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投入；承诺」。

entries.definition: Involvement in wrongdoing with others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「同谋」，只用于坏事。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the noun back to a rolled-up sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个名词系回一张卷好的纸。

normal.en: It is involve plus -ment, the state itself.
normal.cn: 它是 involve 加 -ment，指那个状态本身。

normal.en: You roll into an activity: that is involvement.
normal.cn: 你把自己卷进一项活动，这就是参与。

normal.en: You can roll into trouble just as easily.
normal.cn: 同样容易把自己卷进麻烦里。

normal.en: The -ment turns the act into a lasting condition.
normal.cn: -ment 把动作变成一种持续的状态。

normal.en: Denying involvement is a sentence you hear after scandals.
normal.cn: 丑闻之后总能听到「否认牵连」这句话。

abstract.en: Involvement is the footprint of an interest.
abstract.cn: 参与就是兴趣留下的脚印。

abstract.en: Being inside is warmth and also weight.
abstract.cn: 身在其中，既是温度也是重量。

abstract.en: Once wrapped in, you never unwrap completely.
abstract.cn: 一旦被卷进来，就很难完全卷出去。

examples.en: The school credits its success to parent involvement.
examples.cn: 学校把成功归功于家长的参与。

examples.en: The report found no involvement of local officials.
examples.cn: 报告认定没有当地官员牵涉其中。

examples.en: Her deep involvement with the study left little time for sleep.
examples.cn: 她对这个研究投入极深，几乎没时间睡觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: involve（卷入）+ ment（状态）——被卷进去的那种状态

root: 拉丁语 involvere「卷进去」→ involve → 加 -ment 成 involvement。同族有 involve、involved；形近 investment、involuntary。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: active part, connection to trouble, and emotional commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：主动参与、与麻烦的牵连，以及感情上的投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into a running machine and staying there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进运转的机器并留在里面。

branches.en: THE ROTA: hours written on a board and given away.
branches.cn: 排班表这条线：写在板上、交付出去的时间。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a name placed at a scene of trouble.
branches.cn: 记录这条线：名字被放到出事的地方。

branches.en: THE HEART: a case that will not let go of you.
branches.cn: 心这条线：一个放不下手的案子。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses are a tie between person and event.
branches.cn: 关联这条线：两个义项都是人与事件的连带。

branches.en: THE COST: what you give yourself to takes something back.
branches.cn: 代价这条线：你付出给的事也会取走些什么。

intro.en: Involvement is in- "into", volv- "roll", and -ment naming the state.
intro.cn: involvement 是 in-「进入」、volv-「卷」与标出状态的 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The family rests on Latin volvere and involvere, both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族立足的拉丁语 volvere 与 involvere 均有记载。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的后盾。

items.example: The simplest member of the family.
A cousin that keeps the rolling image.

definition_en: directed towards the inside of something, or happening privately in the mind
core_image: 一支箭头从外面折回，指向自己胸口的方向
scene: 车窗外的城市飞速后退，他不再看风景，目光落在膝盖上的旧照片。A long train ride always turns him inward.
sceneCN: 这里 inward 是「向内、转向内心」（第 2 个义项：注意力回到自己心里），句意为长途坐火车总让他转向内心。画面里的物件：车窗、旧照片、膝上的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：内心的；向内的；内部的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -s 构成，义为「向内地」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在内心」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「内在性」
同构的相反词，义为「向外的」

senses.title: Pointing to the inside
senses.definition: facing or moving towards the centre of something
senses.definitionCN: 朝向或移向某物的中心
senses.example: The door opens with an inward swing.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇门是向内开的。
senses.why: The suffix -weard marks the direction of a turn, as in forward.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -weard 标出转身的方向，正如 forward。

senses.title: Turned to the mind
senses.definition: directed at your own thoughts and feelings rather than at the world outside
senses.definitionCN: 指向自己内心的想法与感受，而非外部世界
senses.example: Her inward life was far busier than her quiet days suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 她的内心生活远比表面安静的日子忙碌。
senses.why: The same arrow was turned from rooms to feelings by later writers.
senses.whyCN: 后世的写作者把同一支箭头从房间转向了感受。

senses.title: Inside a body or building
senses.definition: situated on the inside part of a body or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于身体或建筑结构内侧的
senses.example: The inward wall was damp after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，内墙是潮的。
senses.why: In building and anatomy the word stays physical and means the inner face.
senses.whyCN: 在建筑与解剖里这个词仍指实物，意为内侧的那一面。

intro.en: Inward is a native English compound: the preposition in plus the old suffix -weard, "turned towards".
intro.cn: inward 是英语本土的复合词：介词 in 加上古词尾 -weard「朝向」。

items.en: The word innan meant "within".
items.cn: 古英语 innan 意为「在里面」。

items.en: The suffix -weard meant "turned towards", as in toward.
items.cn: 词尾 -weard 意为「朝向」，与 toward 同源。

items.en: inweard joined them: turned towards the inside.
items.cn: inweard 把两者合起：朝向内的一面。

items.en: Middle English kept inward for the body and the spirit alike.
items.cn: 中古英语用 inward 兼指身体与心灵。

items.en: Modern English added the -ly adverb to mark the mental sense.
items.cn: 现代英语加 -ly 副词来标出心理义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ward direction suffix; the near-meaning group holds words for the inner world.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ward 方向词尾；近义组收表示内在世界的词。

entries.definition: Turned towards the outside.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「向外的」，镜像词。

entries.definition: The adverb form, moving to the inside.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「向内」，同族词。

entries.definition: The one nearer the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」，强调位置。

entries.definition: Happening inside a thing or body.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」，偏客观。

entries.definition: Kept to oneself, not shared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「私人的」，偏不公开。

entries.definition: Habitually looking into one's own mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内省的」，偏习惯。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rely on the -ward ending you already know from forward.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子靠的是你从 forward 里已经认识的 -ward。

normal.en: in plus ward means turned towards the inside.
normal.cn: in 加 ward 就是朝向里面。

normal.en: Forward goes ahead, inward goes in.
normal.cn: forward 向前，inward 向内。

normal.en: An inward door swings into the room.
normal.cn: 向内开的门是朝房间里面转。

normal.en: Its mirror is outward, with the same ending.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是 outward，词尾一样。

normal.en: Turn it on feelings and it means private thought.
normal.cn: 把它对准感受，就指私下的思绪。

abstract.en: Inward is the compass that points at yourself.
abstract.cn: inward 是指向自己的那只罗盘。

abstract.en: Every journey out has a matching journey in.
abstract.cn: 每一趟向外的行程都配一趟向内。

abstract.en: A quiet face can hide the busiest room.
abstract.cn: 安静的脸可以藏住最忙的房间。

examples.en: He gave an inward sigh and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他在心里叹了口气，什么也没说。

examples.en: The inward curve of the bay shelters small boats.
examples.cn: 海湾向内弯，护住了小船。

examples.en: Years of inward reflection made him a patient listener.
examples.cn: 多年的内省使他成了有耐心的倾听者。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ ward（朝向）——朝里面去的

root: 古英语 in「内」+ -weard「朝向」→ inweard → 中古英语 inward。同族有 inwards、inwardly、inwardness；反义 outward。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: pointing inside, turned to the mind, and on the inner side of a body or wall.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：指向内部、转向内心，以及位于身体或墙的内侧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow bent back towards its own chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支折回自己胸口的箭头。

branches.en: THE DOOR: an opening that swings into the room.
branches.cn: 门这条线：朝房间里面转开的入口。

branches.en: THE MIND: attention folded back on itself.
branches.cn: 心灵这条线：注意力折回自身。

branches.en: THE WALL: the side of a structure facing the middle.
branches.cn: 墙这条线：朝向中心的那个面。

branches.en: THE SPACE: both senses are about position and direction.
branches.cn: 空间这条线：两个义项都是位置与方向。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN: what faces inward is not on show.
branches.cn: 隐藏这条线：朝向内侧的东西都不外露。

intro.en: Inward is in- plus the Old English direction suffix -weard.
intro.cn: inward 是 in- 加古英语方向词尾 -weard。

latinIntro.en: This word is native Germanic, so latinEntries stays empty; the Latin cousin is internus.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼本土词，所以 latinEntries 留空；拉丁语里的表亲是 internus。

items.example: It also builds forward and backward.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 forward 与 backward。

items.example: It makes the mirror word outward.
A related form with the same in sense.
A comparative built on the same root.

definition_en: a strong grey metal, a heated tool for smoothing cloth, or the act of pressing clothes with it
core_image: 一块灰黑色的金属锭，旁边放着一台还冒着蒸汽的熨斗
scene: 洗衣房里蒸汽升起，她左手扶着衬衫，右手推着沉重的熨斗走过领口。The old gate is made of iron and has never rusted.
sceneCN: 这里 iron 是「铁」（第 1 个义项：那种金属），句意为这扇老门是铁做的，从来没有生锈。画面里的物件：熨斗、衬衫、蒸汽。

collocations.phrase: strike while the iron is hot

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「熨烫；要熨的衣物」
同以 iron 开头的形近词，义为「反讽」，词源不同
由本词加 ware 构成，义为「铁器」

senses.title: The metal
senses.definition: a hard grey metal used for tools, rails, and gates
senses.definitionCN: 一种坚硬灰暗的金属，用于工具、铁轨与大门
senses.example: The bridge was built with iron beams from the old mill.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥用了旧磨坊拆下来的铁梁。
senses.why: The metal sense is the oldest and stays attached to beams, rails, and gates.
senses.whyCN: 金属义最古老，至今仍与梁、轨、门连在一起。

senses.title: The smoothing tool
senses.definition: a flat heated tool used to press wrinkles out of cloth
senses.definitionCN: 一种扁平且加热的工具，用来压平布上的皱褶
senses.example: The iron was still hot when she put it down.
senses.exampleCN: 她放下熨斗时它还是烫的。
senses.why: The tool took the metal name because it was a block of iron heated over a fire.
senses.whyCN: 这个工具之所以借了金属的名字，因为它本是放在火上加热的铁块。

senses.title: Pressing clothes smooth
senses.definition: to press cloth with heat so that it lies flat
senses.definitionCN: 用热量压平布料
senses.example: He ironed his shirt five minutes before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前五分钟他才把衬衫熨好。
senses.why: The verb is simply the tool turned into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义就是把工具名直接变成动作。

senses.title: Chains and firm will
senses.definition: metal restraints, or metaphorically a hard and unyielding quality
senses.definitionCN: 金属镣铐，或比喻坚硬不屈的性质
senses.example: They spoke of the iron discipline of the mountain rescue team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们谈起山地救援队那种铁一般的纪律。
senses.why: From chains to character, the hard metal became a figure for what will not bend.
senses.whyCN: 从镣铐到性格，这种硬金属成了「不肯弯」的象征。

intro.en: Iron is an old Germanic word; its distant origin is uncertain, though Celtic is a strong candidate.
intro.cn: iron 是个古老的日耳曼词，更远的来源不确定，凯尔特语是较有力的候选。

items.en: The word appears as isern or iren in early texts.
items.cn: 这个词在早期文献中写作 isern 或 iren。

items.en: Related forms include German Eisen and Old Saxon isarn.
items.cn: 同源形式包括德语 Eisen 与古撒克逊语 isarn。

items.en: The deeper root may come from a Celtic metal word, but it is disputed.
items.cn: 更深层词根可能来自凯尔特语的金属词，但仍有争议。

items.en: Middle English changed the -s- to -r-, giving iren.
items.cn: 中古英语把 -s- 变成 -r-，写作 iren。

items.en: Modern English settled on iron for both the metal and the tool.
items.cn: 现代英语把 iron 固定下来，兼指金属与熨斗。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the iron spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for metals and pressing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 iron 拼写；近义组收表示金属与压平动作的词。

entries.definition: Saying the opposite of what you mean.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「反讽」，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: The plural, or chains for a prisoner.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为复数，也可指镣铐。

entries.definition: The activity of pressing clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「熨烫」，同族词。

entries.definition: Iron hardened with carbon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「钢」，铁与碳的合金。

entries.definition: To push down or flatten with force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「压」，压平的动作。

entries.definition: To make a surface even.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「使平整」，结果导向。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie together the metal, the tool, and the act of pressing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把金属、工具和压平这个动作串起来。

normal.en: One word, one metal, one heavy tool.
normal.cn: 一个词，既是金属，也是那件沉工具。

normal.en: An iron is heavy because it is iron.
normal.cn: 熨斗沉，正是因为它就是铁。

normal.en: To iron is to press with that weight.
normal.cn: iron 作动词就是拿这份重量去压。

normal.en: German Eisen is a cousin from the same family.
normal.cn: 德语 Eisen 是同族的表亲。

normal.en: The -r- came late; early English said isern.
normal.cn: 那个 -r- 是后来才有，早先英语说 isern。

abstract.en: Iron is a metal that remembers the shape you give it.
abstract.cn: 铁是会记住你所给形状的金属。

abstract.en: An iron is iron made gentle by heat.
abstract.cn: 熨斗是被热软化过的铁。

abstract.en: Iron will is the metal kept uncooled.
abstract.cn: 铁一般的意志，是不肯冷却的金属。

examples.en: The locket is silver, but the chain is iron.
examples.cn: 坠子是银的，链子却是铁的。

examples.en: She ironed the curtains before hanging them again.
examples.cn: 她先把窗帘熨好再重新挂上。

examples.en: The prisoners wore irons on their ankles.
examples.cn: 囚犯脚踝上带着镣铐。

dict_mnemonic.text: iron 既是铁，也是拿铁做的熨斗，最后成了熨衣服

root: 古英语 isern / iren（日耳曼语词）→ 中古英语 iren → 现代英语 iron。同源有德语 Eisen；更深层来源可能来自凯尔特语，尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the metal, the smoothing tool, pressing clothes, and chains or an unyielding will.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：金属铁、熨斗、熨衣服，以及镣铐或钢铁般的意志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey metal heavy enough to press cloth flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块沉得足以把布压平的灰色金属。

branches.en: THE BEAM: metal bent into bridges and gates.
branches.cn: 铁梁这条线：被弯成桥梁与大门的金属。

branches.en: THE TOOL: the same metal given a handle and heat.
branches.cn: 工具这条线：同一块金属加上把手和热。

branches.en: THE ACT: pressing cloth until wrinkles go.
branches.cn: 动作这条线：把布压到皱褶消失。

branches.en: THE STRENGTH: hardness is both material and metaphor.
branches.cn: 坚硬这条线：硬度既是材质也是比喻。

branches.en: THE HAND: the tool and the act are one idea.
branches.cn: 手这条线：工具和动作本是同一个意思。

intro.en: Iron has no prefix or suffix to cut off; it is a whole Germanic root whose origin is debated.
intro.cn: iron 没有可切分的前后缀，它是一个来源有争议的完整日耳曼词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no secure Latin source, so latinEntries stays empty; Latin ferrum "iron" is unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有可靠的拉丁语来源，所以 latinEntries 留空；拉丁语 ferrum「铁」并不同源。

items.example: It forms irons, also used for chains.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 irons，也用来指镣铐。

items.example: The compound joins iron to ware.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 iron 与 ware 连起来。
另一个复合词，指一种行当。

items.example: It starts with the same letters but is unrelated in origin.
items.exampleCN: 开头字母相同，却不同源。

items.example: The earlier spelling shows the lost -s-.
items.exampleCN: 较早的写法显示那个消失的 -s-。

items.example: The compound keeps the metal image.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了金属的意象。

definition_zh: 宝石；珠宝；珍贵的人或物
definition_en: a precious stone cut and polished for ornament, or something highly valued
core_image: 一束光照进切割好的宝石，里面折出一片细小的彩虹
scene: 老钟表匠把放大镜戴上，从盒子里取出一粒小小的蓝石头嵌进表盘。The crown is set with three jewels.
sceneCN: 这里 jewel 是「宝石」（第 1 个义项：经切割打磨的贵重石料），句意为王冠上镶着三颗宝石。画面里的物件：放大镜、蓝石头、表盘。

pos.zh: 名词：宝石；珠宝；珍贵之物

collocations.zh: 王冠上的明珠；最珍贵的部分

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加 -lery 构成，义为「珠宝首饰」
由本词加 -ler 构成，义为「珠宝商」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「镶有宝石的」
美式拼写的同族词，义为「珠宝」

senses.title: A cut gemstone
senses.definition: a rare stone cut and polished to be worn as ornament
senses.definitionCN: 经切割与打磨、可佩戴作饰的稀有石料
senses.example: The ring holds a single jewel the size of a pea.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚戒指上嵌着一颗豌豆大小的宝石。
senses.why: The stone sense is the base; everything else in the word grows from it.
senses.whyCN: 石头义是根底，这个词的其余用法都从它长出来。

senses.title: Jewellery as a whole
senses.definition: ornaments set with such stones, often kept as family property
senses.definitionCN: 镶有此类石料的饰物，常被当作家产保管
senses.example: The jewels were hidden under the floor for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这些珠宝在地板下面藏了三十年。
senses.why: In the plural the word shifts from one stone to the whole collection.
senses.whyCN: 用复数时，词义从单颗石头转到整批首饰。

senses.title: Something precious
senses.definition: a person or thing that is greatly valued for its quality
senses.definitionCN: 因品质而被人极为看重的人或物
senses.example: The little library is the jewel of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小图书馆是镇上的宝贝。
senses.why: The metaphor is generous: any great thing can be called a jewel.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很宽容：任何出色的东西都能叫 jewel。

intro.en: Jewel reached English through Old French, and its deeper root is debated: game or grace are the usual candidates.
intro.cn: jewel 经由古法语进入英语，更深的词根有争议，常见说法是「玩物」或「恩典」。

items.en: A late Latin word jocale meant "plaything", from jocus, "joke".
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 意为「玩物」，来自 jocus「玩笑」。

items.en: French turned it into jouel, "a precious ornament".
items.cn: 法语把它变成 jouel「贵重饰物」。

items.en: Anglo-Norman carried the word into English records.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语把这个词带入英语文献。

items.en: Middle English wrote it as juel or jewell.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 juel 或 jewell。

items.en: The spelling settled on jewel, and the "precision" metaphor grew.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 jewel，随后又长出「珍贵之物」的比喻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the j- and -el outline; the near-meaning group holds words for precious things.
note.cn: 形近组共用 j- 与 -el 的外形；近义组收表示珍品的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling for ornaments.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珠宝」，美式拼写。

entries.definition: A person who sells jewels.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珠宝商」，同族词。

entries.definition: Decorated with gems.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「镶宝石的」，同族词。

entries.definition: A precious stone, especially cut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「宝石」，最常用近义词。

entries.definition: A hard round body formed inside an oyster.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珍珠」，来自贝壳。

entries.definition: Valuable objects or something deeply valued.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珍宝」，范围更广。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the stone to the plaything it once meant.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把宝石连到它早先「玩物」的意思上。

normal.en: Late Latin jocale meant a plaything.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 意为玩物。

normal.en: A thing of play turned into a thing of price.
normal.cn: 玩物变成了有价钱的东西。

normal.en: One stone is a jewel; many are jewellery.
normal.cn: 一颗叫 jewel，一串叫 jewellery。

normal.en: The seller of them is a jeweller.
normal.cn: 卖它的人叫 jeweller。

normal.en: Anything lovely enough gets called a jewel.
normal.cn: 任何足够可爱的东西都能被叫作 jewel。

abstract.en: Jewels are light trained to stay in one place.
abstract.cn: 宝石是被训练得停在一处的光。

abstract.en: Value is cut into a stone by patience.
abstract.cn: 价值是被耐心一道一道切进石头里的。

abstract.en: A good librarian is a jewel nobody puts in a case.
abstract.cn: 好馆员是不进匣子的宝石。

examples.en: The jeweller set the stone in a thin gold band.
examples.cn: 珠宝商把宝石镶在细金环上。

examples.en: She wore no jewels, only her mother's watch.
examples.cn: 她没戴珠宝，只戴着母亲的手表。

examples.en: The old bridge is the jewel of the river walk.
examples.cn: 这座老桥是沿河步道上最珍贵的一段。

dict_mnemonic.text: jewel 由 jouel 而来，本是「玩物」，后来成了宝石

root: 晚期拉丁语 jocale「玩物」← jocus「玩笑」→ 古法语 jouel「贵重饰物」→ 盎格鲁-诺曼语 → 中古英语 juel → 现代英语 jewel。同族有 jewellery、jeweller、jeweled。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a single cut stone, ornaments as a collection, and anything highly valued.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：单颗切割宝石、成串的珠宝首饰，以及任何极受珍视之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light folded inside a cut stone into a small rainbow.
core.cn: 核心意象：光在切割好的石头里折成一道小彩虹。

branches.en: THE STONE: one cut gem waiting for a setting.
branches.cn: 石头这条线：一颗等着镶座的刻面宝石。

branches.en: THE CASE: a family box of ornaments.
branches.cn: 首饰盒这条线：一只装家传饰物的匣子。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: a place or person worth more than money.
branches.cn: 赞誉这条线：比钱更值的地方或人。

branches.en: THE HAND: both senses pass from hand to hand.
branches.cn: 手这条线：两个义项都靠人与人相传。

branches.en: THE KEEPING: what is precious gets locked away and pointed at.
branches.cn: 珍藏这条线：珍品既被锁起，也被指给人看。

intro.en: Jewel is borrowed whole from French; the added endings are the learnable parts.
intro.cn: jewel 是从法语整体借来的，只有后面加的词尾是能拆的部分。

latinIntro.en: Latin jocale sits behind the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jocale 是法语词的前身。

items.example: It marks the word as a little object.
It forms jewelled, set with gems.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jewelled，镶有宝石的。

items.example: The root points to play, not wealth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指的是玩，不是财富。

definition_en: a person who writes news stories or reports events for a newspaper, magazine, or broadcast service
core_image: 一个人抱着本子挤在人群最前面，边问边记
scene: 雨里围着警戒线，几个人举着手机和录音笔追问路人。A journalist asked the same question three different ways.
sceneCN: 这里 journalist 是「记者」（第 1 个义项：为媒体采写报道的人），句意为一位记者把同一个问题换着问了三种说法。画面里的物件：录音笔、本子、警戒线。

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加 -ism 构成，义为「新闻业」
由本词词干加 -ic 构成，义为「新闻的」
由词根直接构成，义为「期刊；日记」
同源于 jour「日」的形近词，义为「旅程」

senses.title: Reporter for the news
senses.definition: a person whose job is to gather facts and write or broadcast the news
senses.definitionCN: 以收集事实并写成或播出新闻为职业的人
senses.example: A journalist from the local paper rang to check the date.
senses.exampleCN: 当地报纸的一位记者打电话来核对日期。
senses.why: The word grew out of journal, a daily record, so a journalist is literally a day-writer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 journal「每日记录」长出来，字面上就是「写日子的人」。

senses.title: Writer of opinion and features
senses.definition: a person who writes longer pieces, comment, or interviews for a publication
senses.definitionCN: 为刊物撰写长文、评论或访谈的人
senses.example: She works as a journalist for a monthly science magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家科学月刊做撰稿人。
senses.why: As papers grew, the job widened from daily reports to any written news work.
senses.whyCN: 随着报纸增多，这个职业从每日报道扩展到各种文字新闻工作。

intro.en: Journalist is journal, "a daily record", plus -ist; its root is the Latin word for day.
intro.cn: journalist 是 journal「每日记录」加 -ist，其词根是拉丁语的「日」。

items.en: dies meant "day".
items.cn: dies 意为「日」。

items.en: diurnalis meant "daily".
items.cn: diurnalis 意为「每日的」。

items.en: jour kept the day sense; journal named a daily book.
items.cn: jour 保留「日」，journal 指每日的记录簿。

items.en: English used journal for a daily paper.
items.cn: 英语用 journal 指日报。

items.en: The -ist ending marked the person who wrote for it.
items.cn: -ist 词尾标出为它写作的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journ- stem; the near-meaning group holds news jobs by medium.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journ- 词干；近义组按媒介区分新闻行当。

entries.definition: The work or industry of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「新闻业」，同词干。

entries.definition: A trip from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「旅程」，同「日」词根。

entries.definition: Typical of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「新闻式的」，同词干。

entries.definition: One who gathers and reports news.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「记者」，偏出镜与现场。

entries.definition: A reporter based in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「驻外记者」，强调常驻。

entries.definition: One who prepares and approves copy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「编辑」，对稿件加工。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the day in the middle of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「日」留在词的正中间。

normal.en: French jour means day.
normal.cn: 法语 jour 就是「日」。

normal.en: A journal is a book written by the day.
normal.cn: journal 是逐日写下的本子。

normal.en: A journalist writes for the daily.
normal.cn: journalist 就是给日报写东西的人。

normal.en: -ist marks the person, -ism marks the trade.
normal.cn: -ist 指人，-ism 指这一行。

normal.en: Journalism is what the journalist does.
normal.cn: journalism 是 journalist 所做的事。

abstract.en: A journalist is a witness who files copy.
abstract.cn: 记者是交稿的目击者。

abstract.en: The day is the unit; the story is the product.
abstract.cn: 单位是日，产品是故事。

abstract.en: A good reporter asks boring questions until something breaks.
abstract.cn: 好记者一直问无聊的问题，直到有东西裂开。

examples.en: The journalist spent a week on the same street.
examples.cn: 这位记者在同一条街上待了一周。

examples.en: Two journalists were refused entry to the meeting.
examples.cn: 两名记者被拒绝进入会场。

examples.en: She moved from local radio to print journalism.
examples.cn: 她当地电台转做纸质新闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: journal（日报）+ ist（人）——给日报写字的人

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnalis「每日的」→ 古法语 journal「每日记录」→ 英语 journal + -ist → journalist。同族有 journalism、journalistic、journey。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: a news reporter, and a writer of longer pieces or columns.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：采写新闻的记者，以及撰写长文或专栏的撰稿人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone standing at the front of a crowd, asking and writing.
core.cn: 核心意象：挤在人群最前面、边问边写的人。

branches.en: THE NOTEBOOK: notes taken in the street.
branches.cn: 本子这条线：在街上记下的字。

branches.en: THE COLUMN: longer pieces written at a desk.
branches.cn: 专栏这条线：在书桌前写成的长文。

branches.en: THE DEADLINE: both senses live by the daily clock.
branches.cn: 截稿这条线：两个义项都跟着日内的钟走。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: both senses depend on someone who talked.
branches.cn: 消息源这条线：两个义项都要有人开口。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: writing is measured in days, not hours.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：写稿是按天算，不按小时算。

intro.en: Journalist is journ- "day" plus -al and the person-ending -ist.
intro.cn: journalist 是 journ-「日」加 -al，再加指人的 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin dies and diurnalis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dies 与 diurnalis 均有记载。

items.example: The root also appears in journey.
It forms journal, a daily book.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 journal，每日的本子。

items.example: A near synonym with a Latin source.

definition_zh: 关节；接缝；共同的；合办的
definition_en: a place where two parts of a body or structure are connected, or something shared by two or more people
core_image: 两根木条在拐角处被一个榫头接住，那儿可以弯
scene: 木工把两根长条拼成一张矮凳，接头处特意留了一点松动。The table is held together by wooden joints, no nails.
sceneCN: 这里 joint 是「接缝」（第 2 个义项：两个构件相接的部位），句意为这张桌子靠木接缝拼成，不用一根钉子。画面里的物件：木条、榫头、矮凳。

pos.zh: 名词：关节；接缝；大块烤肉

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「共同地」
同词根的动词，义为「连接；加入」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「有关节的」
加前缀 dis- 构成，义为「脱节的；不连贯的」

senses.title: A body joint
senses.definition: the place where two bones meet and allow movement
senses.definitionCN: 两块骨头相接并能活动的地方
senses.example: He hurt the joint of his thumb in the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他的拇指关节被门夹伤了。
senses.why: Anatomy used the word first in English, for the points where bones meet.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最先用它的就是解剖，指骨头相接的地方。

senses.title: A place where parts meet
senses.definition: the point where two pieces of wood or metal are fitted together
senses.definitionCN: 两块木头或金属相嵌合的地方
senses.example: The pipe leaked at the joint near the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那根管子靠墙的接头处漏水。
senses.why: Carpenters and plumbers borrowed the same word for made joins.
senses.whyCN: 木匠和水管工借同一个词来说人造的接合。

senses.title: Shared by two or more
senses.definition: made or held together by two or more parties
senses.definitionCN: 由两方或多方一起做或一起持有的
senses.example: They run a joint shop and split the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合开一家店，房租分摊。
senses.why: The adjective sense moves from physical joining to shared ownership.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义从物理连接挪到共同拥有。

senses.title: A large cut of meat
senses.definition: a piece of meat for roasting, usually with the bone still in
senses.definitionCN: 用于烤制的一块肉，通常带骨
senses.example: Sunday meant a joint of beef and a long table.
senses.exampleCN: 星期天意味着一条烤牛腿和一张长餐桌。
senses.why: A roast joint is the piece carved at the table, where the family joins.
senses.whyCN: 烤大块肉是要在桌上切开的那块，一家人正是在那儿连起来。

intro.en: Joint comes from Latin junctus, "joined", the past participle of jungere, "to join".
intro.cn: joint 来自拉丁语 junctus「已连接的」，是 jungere「连接」的过去分词。

items.en: jungere meant "to join, to yoke together".
items.cn: jungere 意为「连接、套上轭」。

items.en: The past participle junctus meant "joined".
items.cn: 过去分词 junctus 意为「已连接的」。

items.en: French turned it into joint, naming the place of meeting.
items.cn: 法语把它变成 joint，指相接之处。

items.en: Middle English used joint for bones and for carpentry.
items.cn: 中古英语用 joint 指骨头与木作。

items.en: The shared sense grew from "joined together" into business use.
items.cn: 「连在一起」逐渐扩展出商务上的「共同」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the join- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for connections and sharing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 join- 词干；近义组收表示连接与共有的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to connect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「连接」，同词根。

entries.definition: Together, by two or more parties.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「共同地」，同族词。

entries.definition: Lacking connection or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不连贯的」，加前缀 dis-。

entries.definition: A line where two pieces are sewn or joined.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「缝」，多指布料。

entries.definition: Used or held by more than one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「共有的」，偏所有权。

entries.definition: Felt or done by each towards the other.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「相互的」，偏态度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word at a point where two things touch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它放在两物相触的那一点上。

normal.en: jungere means join, and junctus means joined.
normal.cn: jungere 是连接，junctus 是已连接。

normal.en: A joint is where the joining shows.
normal.cn: joint 就是接合显现出来的地方。

normal.en: Remove the joint and the parts fall apart.
normal.cn: 把这个接点去掉，部件就散了。

normal.en: Bones, planks, and bank accounts all have joints.
normal.cn: 骨头、木板、银行账户都有「接头」。

normal.en: Jointly means the two are joined in acting.
normal.cn: jointly 就是两方连着一起做。

abstract.en: A joint is the hinge where one thing becomes two.
abstract.cn: 接缝是一物分成两物的那处铰链。

abstract.en: Bodies and agreements both fail at the joint.
abstract.cn: 身体和协议，都容易在连接处出问题。

abstract.en: Shared work bends better than separate work.
abstract.cn: 共同的事，比分开的事更会弯。

examples.en: His ankle joint still aches after the fall.
examples.cn: 摔倒之后他的踝关节还疼。

examples.en: The chair needs a new wooden joint at the back.
examples.cn: 这把椅子的后部需要换一个木接缝。

examples.en: The two cities opened a joint fire service last year.
examples.cn: 两座城市去年开设了合办的消防服务。

dict_mnemonic.text: join（连接）+ t —— 两块东西连起来的那一点

root: 拉丁语 jungere「连接」→ junctus「已连接的」→ 古法语 joint → 中古英语 joint。同族有 join、jointly、junction、conjunction。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a bone joint, a fitted seam, something shared, and a cut of meat.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：骨头关节、构件接缝、共同持有的，以及一大块肉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hinge where two pieces meet and can move.
core.cn: 核心意象：两件东西相接并能活动的那处铰链。

branches.en: THE BODY: bones meeting where movement happens.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：能活动的骨相接处。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: wood and pipe fitted at a seam.
branches.cn: 手艺这条线：木头与管子在缝处相嵌。

branches.en: THE DEAL: two parties holding one thing.
branches.cn: 交易这条线：两方持有一物。

branches.en: THE TABLE: a joint of meat at a shared meal.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：一顿共餐上的一大块肉。

branches.en: THE LINK: all senses are a place where two become one.
branches.cn: 连接这条线：所有义项都是两物合一之处。

intro.en: Joint is the Latin past participle ending -t on the root joining-; the word itself is borrowed whole.
intro.cn: joint 是词根 joining- 加拉丁过去分词词尾 -t，整词直接从法语借来。

latinIntro.en: Latin jungere and junctus are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 与 junctus 均有记载。

items.example: The root also appears in junction and adjoin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 junction 与 adjoin。
它把 junctus 标为「已连接」。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。
这个分词给了 joint 那个 -t。

items.example: Same root with a different ending.

definition_en: an act of travelling from one place to another, especially a long one, or a long process of change
core_image: 一条从地平线开头、一直延伸到看不见尽头的路
scene: 清早的车站，人提着行李站在站台尽头，列车的灯从远处亮起来。The journey takes nine hours if the trains run on time.
sceneCN: 这里 journey 是「旅程」（第 1 个义项：从此地到彼地的行程），句意为如果列车准点，这趟要九个钟头。画面里的物件：行李、站台、列车灯。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「旅行者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「旅行」
同源于 jour「日」的形近词，义为「日记；期刊」

senses.title: Travel from one place to another
senses.definition: an act of travelling, especially over a long distance
